name: Clopidogrel
summary: An antiplatelet prodrug that depends on metabolic activation, which is why genotype and drug interactions matter so much.
good: Secondary prevention and stent-related antiplatelet strategies when it is the right agent.
bad: Patients needing a stronger or more predictable antiplatelet effect without reviewing activation issues.
clinicalPearls: A prodrug that needs activation is only as good as the activation pathway.
mechanism: Irreversibly blocks the platelet P2Y12 receptor after hepatic activation, reducing ADP-driven platelet aggregation.
indications: Post-ACS therapy, after coronary stenting, and secondary prevention of atherothrombotic events.
interactionNotes: Some PPIs, especially omeprazole and esomeprazole, can reduce activation; other bleeding-risk drugs add concern.

warnings: Bleeding risk and variable response in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers are the key issues.
